pipeline_name: Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: Keep this row as the Kyiv to Western Border row and merge P0777 into it. Record the length tension.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. The Ukrtransgaz chronology lists the Kyiv to Western Border of Ukraine gas pipeline: first string 183.6 km, 1020 mm, 1970; second string 216.3 km, 1220 mm, 1972. That gives 399.9 km, which matches the sheet. P0777 describes the same two-string system with a wrong length, so it duplicates this row. Length sources disagree: Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 367 km and 506 km, the Soviet design institute table gives 590 km for the block, and the chronology also lists a 42.8 km piece in 1974. The sheet value follows the operator's own chronology.

verifications.note: Interfax-Ukraine, 21 September 2020: the 1020 mm Kyiv - Western Ukraine high-pressure line near Chabany was repaired and works in normal mode. Names the line as 'Київ - Західна Україна'.

fills.researcher_notes: An Interfax-Ukraine report from September 2020 says the 1020 mm Kyiv to Western Ukraine line ruptured near Chabany and was back in normal operation within days. The page uses the local name Kyiv - Western Ukraine, not the exact sheet name. This is the newest dated evidence found. No source dated 2024 or later that names this line was found, so the tier is medium.
Both pages describe a natural gas trunk line. The Interfax-Ukraine page calls it a high-pressure gas pipeline. The Ukrainian Wikipedia article covers the same system.

fills.researcher_notes: The Ukrtransgaz chronology (read through a June 2025 Wayback capture, because utg.ua blocks automated requests) dates the first string to 1970 and the second string to 1972. One source family only. Ukrainian Wikipedia dates the second string to 1973, which is a one-year difference noted here.

The Ukrtransgaz chronology gives 183.6 km for the first string and 216.3 km for the second. The sum is 399.9 km, which matches the sheet. The same chronology lists a further 42.8 km piece of the Kyiv to Western Border line with 1200 mm pipe, commissioned in 1974, which would bring the total to 442.7 km if it belongs to this corridor. Two other figures conflict. Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 367 km and 506 km for the two strings. A Soviet design institute table gives 590 km for one block. These stay as a documented tension, the sheet value is kept.

fills.researcher_notes: The Ukrtransgaz chronology names Kyiv as the start of the line and the Western Border of Ukraine as the far end. The sheet leaves the end location blank and nothing was added. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the second string joins the Dolyna to Uzhhorod line, which does not support the Drozdovychi end point the wiki suggests.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence found is a September 2020 report that the 1020 mm line was repaired and back in normal mode. No source dated 2024 or later that names this line was found, in Ukrainian or English searches, and the regulator's 2025 to 2034 plan documents checked do not mention it. The sheet status is kept. This is a weak confirm. The line is inside Ukraine west of Kyiv and may carry domestic and storage flows now that Russian transit has ended, but no source says so.

cross_row_leads.facts: Soviet design institute table lists Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv at 522 km, 1000 mm. That 522 km is one half of the 1,112 km on P0777.

summary: "Kyiv-Western Border of Ukraine: real, 399.9 km on Ukrtransgaz chronology, duplicate of P0777; status confirmed weakly (newest evidence 2020)."
